findings.what: web.export refuses ordinary pages. `<a href>` is a navigation carrier (Load::Document, web-assets carriers.rs:577). Its reference reaches Port::resolve even when it names the document itself (assets.rs decide: only reads_text contexts turn a self-spelling into SelfReference). The document's own name comes back Granted, and then `assets.contains(&recipe.file)` refuses export_path_collision. A directory link (`href="/"`, `"./"`, `"docs/"`) fails asset_id at the empty last segment (line 781), so it is Denied and the export refuses asset_denied.
findings.scenario: local_root/index.html holds `Home` (or ``); web.export_recipe output_root=out; web.export refuses export_path_collision (or asset_denied: not_granted: /). The lane's fixture has only `#top` and https links, so its tests pass.
findings.fix: In export, skip a Granted id equal to `port.document` (the document is already written from out_doc). For a navigation-only reference that is the site root or a directory, list it as a link and do not copy or refuse it (Port::resolve already gets `loads`). Alternatively, name the directory-link refusal as a declared cut.

findings.what: A stale site record comes back after undo, save and reopen. save writes the sidecar only when site or recipe is Some, and never removes or clears an existing one.
findings.scenario: web.open P (no sidecar), web.site {...}, web.save overwrite (sidecar written), web.undo (site None, the step survives the save), web.save overwrite (sidecar untouched), web.open P: the undone site is back. The same happens after web.open source=... and web.save to an existing P that has an old sidecar.
findings.fix: When the record is None and sidecar(&path) exists, write sidecar_json(None, None) (read_sidecar already maps nulls to (None, None)) or remove the file.

findings.what: An export collision is caught after files are already written, so a refusal that should change nothing leaves files behind. Collisions are checked case-sensitively (BTreeSet of ids, `assets.contains(&recipe.file)`) and the reserved output names are never checked. On NTFS, two references that differ only in case both resolve (symlink_metadata is case-insensitive) and come back as two ids. write_new then fails on the second one, after the earlier files are on disk.
findings.scenario: On Windows, `` (or an asset `Index.html` beside recipe.file `index.html`, or a referenced `studio-export-manifest.json`): web.export writes Logo.png and the files before it, then refuses export_path_collision. output_root is left non-empty with no manifest, so the next export refuses output_not_empty. A referenced `studio-publish-receipt.json` is overwritten by the next publish, and the publish after that refuses export_changed.
findings.fix: Before the first write, build one ASCII-case-folded set of every output name (asset ids, recipe.file, MANIFEST_FILE, RECEIPT_FILE) and refuse export_path_collision on any duplicate.

findings.what: web.publish can overwrite the site's source files, and its guard against publishing into the export does not hold. The only guard compares target_root with export_root, and it runs only when both paths canonicalize. Nothing compares the target with the site's local_root, and a target that does not exist yet skips the check.
findings.scenario: (a) A local_or_network target with root_path = local_root and a minify recipe: publish replaces local_root/index.html (the open document's file) with the minified export, and state still says dirty:false. (b) root_path = <output_root>/live, not yet created: the first publish writes into the export tree, although the lane notes say a publish root inside the export is refused.
findings.fix: Canonicalize the nearest existing ancestor of target_root. Refuse publish_over_export when it is inside or contains the export root, and refuse a target equal to the canonical local_root or the document's folder.

findings.what: The asset gate can grant a file outside the site root. symlink_metadata checks only the last path component, so a junction or symlink directory inside local_root is followed. The module docs promise 'a regular file under the site root'.
findings.scenario: local_root/media is a junction to C:/Users//Documents and the page has ``: the file is Granted, then copied into the export and published.
findings.fix: In Port::resolve, require canonicalize(join(root,id)).starts_with(canonicalize(root)), otherwise answer Denied.

findings.what: Q5: history.undo after a web edit can undo a different, older step and report success. The two histories do not know about each other. The manual's limit line declares this, but the reply gives no sign of it.
findings.scenario: A package edit (layer.rename), then web.set_text, then history.undo (or a drive `undo` line): the rename is undone, ok:true, and the web edit stays. With no package step, the reply is nothing_to_undo although a web step exists.
findings.fix: Give run steps and web steps a sequence number from one counter on Run. history.undo and history.redo refuse a typed `newest_step_is_web` (hint web.undo) when the web host's newest undo step is newer than the run's newest step. If the lead accepts the documented limit instead, this finding can be dropped.

findings.what: `std::mem::take(&mut run.web)` moves the host out for the call. If anything in execute panics, the drive's catch_unwind (drive.rs:586) keeps the session going with an empty WebHost: document, history, site and recipe are gone, and revision reads 0. The manual promises 'what it had already changed stays changed'.
findings.scenario: Any panic inside hsk_studio_web parse or preview during a web command.
findings.fix: Call `run.web.execute(row, params, &ctx, run.cancel)` directly. The borrows are of disjoint fields, so no take is needed.

answers.q2_dependency_closure: hsk-studio-web -> accord, observe, web-core, web-assets, sha2 =0.10.9 (force-soft); web-core -> accord, observe, sha2; web-assets -> accord, web-core; observe -> accord. None reaches harness-core, so there is no cycle. html5ever is a dev-dependency only. No winit, egui or wgpu. SHA-256 is web-core's sha256_hex over sha2 0.10.9 (cfg-if, cpufeatures 0.2.17, digest 0.10.7), which is already in Cargo.lock and used by hsk-studio-package and the interop crates. The lock diff is the single dependency line. License: the closure is the workspace's own crates plus the sha2/digest family; their license fields were NOT read in this review.
answers.q3_file_system: Asset ids: `..` escape, backslash, absolute, UNC, drive-letter (':' is not portable), dot-leading, reserved device names and over-deep paths are all refused in asset_id/portable. recipe.file is a single portable name. Manifest paths read back are re-checked with asset_id. There is no walk of local_root: only referenced paths are stat'ed. Peak export memory is bounded at about 1 GiB plus one 256 MiB asset. Gaps: F1, F3, F4 and F5. Secrets: the name check is top-level and case-folded, and any other unlisted key is refused parameter_unknown, so nothing slips by name. Through the drive, params_from_text refuses parameter_unknown before the engine's credential_in_site_record, so the code differs from the documented one; the value is not echoed. Value-level secrets (host `user:pw@h`) are not detected, and none is claimed.
answers.q4_span_rewrite: apply sorts the edits stably by (start, end), and patched() sorts the forward edits the same way before zipping them with Applied.changed, so the inverse spans line up, including zero-width inserts at one position and adjacent deletions. UTF-8 boundaries are checked by apply. Quoting and escaping are engine code (set_attribute requotes an unquoted value when it needs it), unchanged at base. Undo after save works in-process; reopen clears the history, as the docs say. Only F2 is wrong across save and reopen.
